title: 2024 Energy Consumption Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report presents the findings from the analysis of 2024 smart-meter data, focusing on total and per-building-type electricity usage, quarterly trends, half-year changes, commercial load on hot days, and the distribution of consumption and temperature. Key findings include a 4.71% increase in energy consumption from the first to the second half of the year, with industrial buildings accounting for the majority of usage. The analysis also reveals a negative correlation between temperature and commercial energy consumption on hot days.

key_findings.statement: The total energy consumption for 2024 was 1,207,699.96 kWh, with an average of 845.73 kWh per reading across 1,428 readings.
Energy consumption varied significantly by building type, with Industrial (995,362.16 kWh) > Commercial (196,367.15 kWh) > Residential (15,970.65 kWh).
Quarterly energy consumption showed a trend of Q4 (352,881.81 kWh) > Q1 (319,677.67 kWh) > Q2 (270,277.36 kWh) > Q3 (264,863.12 kWh).
There was a 4.71% increase in energy consumption from the first half (589,955.03 kWh) to the second half (617,744.93 kWh) of the year.
On hot days (temperature >= 25°C), commercial buildings had 19 readings with an average consumption of 415.29 kWh.

The median energy consumption was 406.8 kWh with a standard deviation of 913.44 kWh. The mean temperature was 11.61°C, with 62 readings having missing temperature data. Commercial energy consumption showed a negative correlation (-0.638) with temperature.

Energy consumption was nearly evenly split between peak (599,624.07 kWh, 49.65%) and off-peak (608,075.89 kWh) periods. There were 12 unique meters, with the highest usage meter consuming 252,241.26 kWh.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single year of data, which may not capture long-term trends.
Missing temperature data for 62 readings could affect the accuracy of temperature-related findings.
The correlation between temperature and commercial energy consumption is based on a limited number of hot-day readings.
conclusion: The analysis provides valuable insights into 2024 energy consumption patterns, highlighting the dominance of industrial usage, seasonal variations, and the impact of temperature on commercial energy consumption. Future analyses should consider longer time frames and address data limitations to enhance accuracy and reliability.
